answer.line: The Calvin cycle spends ATP and NADPH and sends the empties, ADP and NADP+, back to be recharged.

steps: Here is the loop: the light reactions charge carriers, and the Calvin cycle spends them.
A spent ATP is ADP plus phosphate. A spent NADPH is NADP+.
Those empties go back to the thylakoid to be recharged. Stall either trip and the other stops within seconds.

choices.note: The empty carriers, heading back to be recharged.
CO2 comes in from the air and G3P leaves to become sugar. Neither one goes back to the thylakoid.
Water is split at the thylakoid and oxygen leaves the leaf. The Calvin cycle sends neither one back.
These are the charged carriers that arrive at the Calvin cycle. The stem asks what goes back.
Phosphate does go back, riding with ADP. Glucose is built from G3P after it leaves the cycle and never returns.

lockIt: Charged carriers, ATP and NADPH, go to the stroma; the empties, ADP and NADP+, come back.
hook: Full trucks out, empty trucks back.

visual.alt: Two boxes, the light reactions in the thylakoid and the Calvin cycle in the stroma, joined by four arrows. ATP and NADPH run out to the Calvin cycle; ADP plus phosphate and NADP+ run back, drawn in green as the answer. Water, oxygen, carbon dioxide and G3P stay on their own sides.
visual.caption: Read the green arrows pointing back to the thylakoid. Those are the empties.
